title: Trace attestation & metric heuristics walkthrough
body:
Summary:

This doc is a working walkthrough for two interlinked efforts: (1) trace attestation — a lightweight scheme to mark/validate spans as authoritative for specific latency/quality signal derivation, and (2) metric heuristics — a small set of proven rules for deriving operational metrics from raw traces and batches in the inference runtime. Goal is to reduce ambiguity for dashboard owners and to make investigation steps reproducible across teams.

Context and motivation (short):
- Our current dashboards sometimes disagree when investigating a regression: host-level metrics, per-request metrics, and trace-derived latencies don't always align because of sampling, aggregation windows, and non-deterministic KV cache effects.
- Operators spend 30–60m reconciling traces to metrics during incidents. We should narrow that down with a deterministic attestation surface and compact heuristics that translate traces -> SLI-friendly metrics.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Minimal span annotations for attestation (what fields to add, semantics)
- Heuristics for generating per-request metrics (TTFT, model-queue-time, kv-warmth-index)
- Dashboard tile recommendations (compact, investigation-first wiring)
- Short operator playbook snippets and a checklist for signal validation during rollouts

Principles:
- Keep attestation lightweight: avoid heavy payloads on every span. Prefer tags/flags with small cardinality.
- Conservative derivations: default to under-counting rather than double-counting (better to miss some tokens than inflate SLI).
- Reproducible transforms: a single reference SQL/Notebook should reconstruct every dashboard value.

Trace attestation spec (proposal):
Fields to add to relevant spans (encoder/decoder/kvcache/request-router):
- span.attested = {"none" | "partial" | "full"}  -- textual, low-cardinality
- span.role = {"request", "kernel", "kv-prefetch", "kv-evict", "transport"}
- span.model_variant = string (short id, e.g., 8-char tag)
- span.seq_len_hint = integer (optional, only present when request includes hint)

Semantics: 
- "full": this span is the authoritative source for a time slice used to build a per-request latency metric. There should be at most one full span per request-level metric anchor.
- "partial": additional work that contributes but should be aggregated carefully (e.g., background kv prefetch).
- "none": default. Means no attestation applied.

Why this pattern:
- With attested anchors we can align trace quantiles and SLI buckets deterministically (no guessing which kernel span to pick).
- Low-cardinality textual flags keep queries cheap.

Metric heuristics (derive per-request metrics from traces):
Heuristic A — Time-To-First-Token (TTFT):
- Anchor: span where span.role=="request" and span.attested=="full"
- TTFT = time from request ingress timestamp to the first child span with role == "kernel" that has produced token=true. If kernel token marker missing, fall back to first kernel span start.
- Sampling: if no attested span present, mark request as 'uncertain' and exclude from 99% SLI but include in 50% with tag uncertain=true for visibility.

Heuristic B — End-to-end latency (E2E):
- Anchor: same attested request span. E2E = attested_span.end - attested_span.start. If multiple attested spans per request, pick the one with role=="request" and most tokens.

Heuristic C — KV Warmth Index (0..1):
- Count prefetched kv hits vs total kv lookups within request trace window (bounded by attested_span).
- Warmth = hits / (hits + misses + 1e-6). Persist as a per-request tag; aggregate to 5th/50th/95th quantiles per model/route.

Heuristic D — Model queue wait (host-side):
- Derive queue_wait = time between request-router queue_enter and kernel queue_dequeue spans (match request-id). If kernel queue_dequeue missing, mark queue_wait=unknown and surface in dashboard tile as gray.

Aggregation rules (important):
- Use request-aware rollups: compute per-request metrics from traces first, then roll up rather than aggregating raw spans. This avoids double-counting when model fanout occurs.
- Quantile alignment: when mapping trace quantiles to dashboard panels, always compute quantiles over per-request aggregates; do not mix span-level quantiles with request-level ones.

Dashboard wiring suggestions (investigation-first):
- Primary pane: compact scatter of per-request TTFT vs E2E colorized by kv-warmth-index. X=TTFT, Y=E2E, color=warmth. Allows quick triage for requests with high TTFT but normal E2E (indicates early kernel stalls) vs high E2E and low TTFT (post-processing / transport).
- Top row: 95th E2E (%), 99th TTFT (ms), 95th queue_wait, false_positive_rate (for regen triggers).
- Drilldown: link each point to trace explorer with pre-applied query filter attested=="full" and request_id=<id>.
- Failure heatmap: tenant x model_variant with cell showing p95 E2E and a small sparkline of kv-warmth.

Operator playbook snippets (short):
- If p95 TTFT spikes but E2E stable -> look for increased kernel startup spans or increased seq_len_hint variability.
- If kv-warmth drops for a tenant -> check prefetch probe success rates and tenant affinity routing changes.
- If queue_wait rises across hosts -> investigate autoscaler/backpressure settings for Dedicated pools.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Attestation propagation for fanout requests: should child requests inherit 'full' or be 'partial'? (current lean: child requests stay partial, parent attests full; will break some multi-model flows)
- Cardinality risk: model_variant id needs canonical short form; propose 8-char stable tag — does product already expose this?
- Storage/retention impact: per-request warmth index + tags will increase trace size; need to estimate 6–12% overhead. Ops to estimate on sample day.

Small experiment plan (2-week):
Week 1: instrument: add span.attested tagging in runtime (encoder/router) for a single small model (gpt-lite-8b), and emit kv-prefetch spans with role tags. Toggle behind experimental flag.
Week 2: collect traces for internal sandbox traffic; implement notebook to reconstruct per-request aggregates and validate heuristics vs manual trace picking for 200 samples.

Acceptance criteria for rollout:
- Notebook reproduces dashboard numbers to within 1% for p50 and 3% for p95 on the sandbox sample set.
- Dashboard queries run within 2s for 7d window for the sample tenant traffic.
- Ops runbook includes at least 3 concrete triage steps that reduce median investigation time by 20% in a table-top drill.

Short TODO list:
- [ ] Add attested flag to router spans (owner: @Luis) — target PR: GH:instrumentation#128
- [ ] Shorten model_variant to 8-char stable tag (owner: @Mei) — RFC follow-up RFC-451
- [ ] Notebook reconstructing per-request metrics (owner: @Aisha) — link to notebook in linked_artifacts once ready
- [ ] Dashboard prototype tile (owner: @Jordan) — attach to dashboard id: OBS-DASH-74

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep sample_size for p95 validation >= 200 across tenants.
- When in doubt about missing spans, surface 'uncertain' flag so queries can exclude them easily.
- Communicate changes in instrumentation via #observability and add short changelog entry.

Appendix (quick examples):
- Example trace filter to compute per-request E2E in analytics: SELECT request_id, MAX(span_end)-MIN(span_start) FROM traces WHERE span.attested='full' GROUP BY request_id
- Example warmth SQL: SELECT request_id, SUM(kv_hit::int)/NULLIF(SUM(kv_hit::int)+SUM(kv_miss::int),0) as warmth FROM traces WHERE span.role IN ('kv-prefetch','kv-access') AND request_window GROUP BY request_id

If you pick this up: start by reviewing the attestation semantics and the model_variant tagging because both are low-effort and unlock deterministic rollups. We'll iterate on heuristics after we have 1 model's traces instrumented.

-- Aisha
